lines.trans: His grandfather used to slice warm lemon cake with powdered sugar on top!
Oh! The yellow lemon cake, we used to fight over the corner piece every Friday!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

meanings.note: Exclamation of mild surprise or realization ('oh!').

examples.trans: Oh! My glasses are on my head!
Oh, look at the beauty of this ceiling!

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستقبل, بيستقبل).

examples.trans: Let us go down to welcome the new guest.
They welcomed us with a smile and hot tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستنى, بيستنى).

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيانوهات.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخانق, بيتخانق).

examples.trans: We used to argue over the corner piece!
We fell out over selling the old house.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ثواني.

examples.trans: Wait one second, please.
He came back ten seconds later on the dot.

meanings.note: Means 'grandfather' (جدي my grandfather) and in عن جد ('really / seriously') means 'earnestness'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: Everyday counting unit for rolls of bread, fruit, lemons, or pills (خدي حبة take a piece; ست حبات ليمون six lemons).

examples.trans: Take a bread roll while it is hot.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Used warmly across ages in Jordan: يا حبيبي (to a boy/man, or as 'my goodness!') and يا حبيبتي (to a girl/woman).

examples.trans: Good morning, my dear.
A warm welcome to dear friends.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبز, بيخبز).

examples.text: اخبزي قطع زوايا كتير يا سلمى!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, Salma!

examples.text: قديش بيقدر فرنك يخبز كل صبح؟
examples.trans: How much can your oven bake every morning?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

meanings.note: Used mainly in polite/earnest requests: أرجوك (to a man), أرجوكي (to a woman), أرجوكم (plural) — 'please!'.

examples.trans: Please write down that sentence!
Please do not open the white parcel.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: زوايا.

examples.trans: The corner shop opens early.
I love the corner pieces of lemon cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Numeral 'six'; short form ست (sitt) before a plural noun (ست سنين 'six years').

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.
We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سلال.

examples.trans: I put the yellow lemons in the basket.
He tossed the paper into the wastebasket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

examples.trans: Everything is ready on the table.

examples.text: رن الجرس إذا احتجت أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Warm, reassuring 'of course! / naturally!'.

examples.trans: Of course, Tariq, your secret is safe with us!
Of course I came when I got your card.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Pronounced duhur in everyday Jordanian: الظهر means 'at noon / midday'.

examples.trans: He will arrive Friday at noon.
The sun is high at midday.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغلب, بيغلب).

examples.trans: Please do not trouble yourself on our account!
Sorry if I put you to trouble today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغلط, بيغلط).

examples.text: لما يغلط بنغمة بيانو كان يكشر!
examples.trans: Whenever he missed a piano note, he would frown!

examples.text: كل واحد ممكن يغلط بأول يوم.
examples.trans: Anyone can make a mistake on the first day.

meanings.note: Adverb 'right away, at once'.

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading out right away!
The hot water came back immediately.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاسية, plural: قاسيين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني بس!
examples.trans: He used to act tough for just five seconds!
Amman's winter cold is sometimes harsh.

meanings.note: Asks price, quantity, or time (قديش الساعة؟ 'what time is it?') and exclaims degree (قديش هادية! 'how peaceful!').

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قطع.

examples.trans: Please have a piece of warm bread.

examples.text: خبزت كيكة مع قطع زوايا زيادة.
examples.trans: She baked a cake with extra corner pieces.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقطع, بيقطع).

examples.text: جدي كان يقطع كيكة ليمون دافية.
examples.trans: My grandfather used to slice warm lemon cake.
Salma sliced the hot bread.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكشر, بيكشر).

examples.text: لما يغلط بالنغمة كان يكشر عالحيط!
examples.trans: When he missed a note, he used to scowl at the wall!
Do not frown, smile!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

كمان.gloss: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)

meanings.en: also; too; again (كمان مرة once more)
meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for 'also, too, more' (كمان مرة 'one more time / again').

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلين, بيلين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني وبعدين يلين!
examples.trans: He would act tough for five seconds and then soften up!
His kind heart softens quickly.

meanings.note: Means 'still' in affirmative sentences (لسا سليم 'still intact') and 'not yet' alone or with negation (لسا؟ 'not yet?').

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلف, بيلف).

examples.text: لفي شمال برا البوابة وامشي دغري.
examples.trans: Turn left outside the gate and walk straight.
Turn left at the stair landing.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: متذكرة, plural: متذكرين).

examples.trans: Do you still remember that story after all these years?
I remember the building number well.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مرات.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين).

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Clear, polite 'yes' (slightly warmer and more formal than casual آه).

examples.trans: Yes, room four is on the second floor!
Yes, a hundred times yes!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: نغمات.

examples.text: سمع كل نغمة من البيانو بهدوء.
examples.trans: He listened quietly to every note of the piano.
The chime of the bell is gentle, not harsh.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أيام.

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!
